title: Task-Aware Adaptive KV Cache Compression
one_line_claim: Adaptively compresses KV cache to task characteristics by adjusting per-layer token retention budgets during inference.
method_summary: DynamicKV establishes global and per-layer KV cache budgets, temporarily retaining the maximum budget for the current layer while periodically updating cache sizes across all preceding layers during inference. The method adapts token retention strategies to task-specific activation patterns observed across transformer layers.

key_findings.finding: Retains only 1.7% of full KV cache while achieving approximately 85% of full KV cache performance on LongBench.
key_findings.quote: retains only 1.7% of the KV cache size while achieving ~85% of the Full KV cache performance on LongBench

key_findings.finding: Under extreme compression (0.9%), surpasses state-of-the-art methods by 11% in Needle-in-a-Haystack testing with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2.
key_findings.quote: under extreme compression (0.9%), DynamicKV surpasses state-of-the-art methods by 11% in the Needle-in-a-Haystack test using Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2

key_findings.finding: Observes distinct activation patterns across layers in various tasks, demonstrating that different tasks require different compression strategies at different model depths.
key_findings.quote: distinct activation patterns across layers in various tasks

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV-cache compression in LLMs and evaluate performance on long-context tasks; both consider per-layer or per-token granularity in compression decisions.
differs_on: DynamicKV uses task-aware activation pattern analysis to guide compression decisions; HERALD predicts catastrophic failures from per-token logit features post-hoc.
DynamicKV is a proactive compression strategy that adapts budgets during inference; HERALD is a failure detection mechanism that warns about compression-induced hazards.
DynamicKV optimizes for performance retention under compression; HERALD specifically targets catastrophic failure modes (looping, non-termination).
